answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it may trade, then slash that deposit when a challenge proves coordinated abuse. A rotating committee selects challenges from a public beacon, and agents commit to answers with a cipher before revealing them, making copied responses detectable. An island of accounts under common control still needs separate capital per identity; faking a thousand agents therefore ties up funds and risks losing them, while a violet badge alone grants no trust.
